messages.author: b647a89a4db2f284
messages.subject: Multi-Group SEM; labels, equality constraints
parts:
In fitting the following multi-group model with lavaan is there a to combine 1) selectively setting regression coefficients to zero in some groups and 2) labeling of regression coefficients (which allows setting regression coefficients equal across groups)?

med_group.model <- '
M1 ~ c(a1,a1,a1,a1)*X1 +  c(a2,a2,a2,a2)*X2 + c(a3,a3,a3,a3)*X3 + c(a4,a4,a4,a4)*X4
M2  ~ c(a5,a5,a5,a5)*X1 + c(a6,a6,a6,a6)*X2 + c(a7,a7,a7,a7)*X3 + c(a8,a8,a8,a8)*X4 + c(a9,a9_1,a9_1,a9_1)*M1
y   ~ c(NA,0,NA,NA)*X1 + c(NA,0,0,0)*X2 + c(NA, NA, NA, NA)*X3 + c(NA, NA, NA, 0)*X4 + c(0,NA,NA,NA)*M1 + c(NA, NA, NA, NA)*M2 + c(0,NA,0,NA)*M1:M2
'
fitmedsem_group <- sem(med_group.model, df, group = "Group.factor")

By using the syntax "c(NA,0,NA,NA)*X1", I can set the regression coefficient of X1 equal to 0 in g2 ("group.2") while allowing it to vary freely for g1, g3, and g4.
By using the syntax "c(a1,a1,a1,a1)*X1", I can set the regression coefficients of X1 equal across g1, g2, g3, g4.

But when I try to combine the two notations, e.g. by "c(a1,0,a1,a1)*X1" I get an error:

"wrong number of arguments in modifier (a1,a1,a1) of element y~X1"

...and if I try to fix it by e.g., "c("a1",0,"a1","a1")*X1", then '0' is treated as a name of the regression coefficient of X1 in g2, instead of being an instruction to set the regression coefficient of X1 equal to 0 in g2, as the notation "c(NA,0,NA,NA)*X1" allows.

Thanks!

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: Multi-Group SEM; labels, equality constraints
parts:
Neils,
  In the first case, you started giving lavaan a vector of labels.  Mixing labels and values in the same vector is not allowed.  So, lavaan made a reasonable assumption that the entire vector contained names.

  In the second case, lavaan matches value to groups based on position.  If you do not fill all four positions, lavaan has no way to know which values are meant for which groups.  So, lavaan asked for four values.

  You can provide both a label vector and a value vector for the same variable (technically for the same parameter).  See the last two sections of the model.syntax help file for details.  Here is a runable example using both a label vector and a value vector for the effect of x7 on x1.  A2 = 0, B2 is free.  Duplicate labels would fix the parameter across groups but the data only had two groups.  So, I illustrated that with x4 instead.

summary(HolzingerSwineford1939)

myModel <- '
  x1 ~ 1 + c(A1,A1)*x4 + c(0, NA)*x7 + c(A2, B2)*x7
  x1 ~~ x1
' # end myModel

lavaanify(myModel, ngroups = 2)

myFit <- lavaan(myModel, data=HolzingerSwineford1939, group='school')
summary(myFit)

You can confirm the desired result in the summary output.

With four groups, you can use vectors such as c(0, NA, NA, NA) and c(A1, B1, B1, B1).  In that case A1 is fixed to 0 and B1 is free but subject to equality constraints.

Keith

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: Multi-Group SEM; labels, equality constraints
parts:
Carl,
  I do not see anything wrong with your approach.  The approach that I described might be considered more standard because it has been part of lavaan model syntax longer.  You are using a feature that was added more recently for a different purpose.  I think that the primary advantage to the older approach is that it keeps all the relevant parts of the syntax close together.  The reader does not need to make connections between potentially disparate lines.  I do not believe that there should be any difference in terms of performance.

  Subjective judgments of simplicity are easily influenced by familiarity and are perhaps therefore at least to some extent a matter of taste.  All use of model syntax in lavaan is just a wrapper for parameter tables that concedes some indirection in exchange for a more intuitive interface.  In one sense of 'simple', then, skipping the model syntax and directly specifying the parameter table would always be simpler than any model syntax solution.  In this sense, we are all choosing to give up simplicity for something else when we use model syntax because it could be eliminated entirely.

Keith
